boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Documented University of Nevada, Reno rituals, school songs, annual events and historic practices—presented with current-status caveats where the source does not confirm an upcoming occurrence.

cards.title: Refresh the giant Peavine Peak N
cards.subtitle: Peavine Peak above the University of Nevada, Reno
cards.notes: Watch ASUN announcements for summer volunteer recruitment, then join the supervised refresh rather than attempting to visit or paint the landmark independently.
cards.short_summary: Students have refreshed the large white N since its 1913 creation.
cards.evidence_claim: Students formed the 140-by-150-foot N in 1913; ASUN now recruits summer volunteers to refresh it for volunteer hours.
cards.access_notes: Participate only through an announced ASUN volunteer opportunity; the source describes summer recruitment.

cards.title: Attend the spring Powwow respectfully
cards.subtitle: University of Nevada, Reno campus
cards.notes: Check the University calendar for the spring program, follow event guidance, and make time for the regalia, dance and music presented with local Native communities.
cards.short_summary: A campus Powwow honors graduates and celebrates higher education.
cards.evidence_claim: Started by the Native American Student Association in 1991, the Powwow has been held annually since 2005 and is produced with local Native community collaboration.
cards.access_notes: The source identifies this as a spring event; confirm the current program, location and participation guidance before attending.

cards.title: Follow the blue-or-red cannon rivalry
cards.subtitle: Nevada Wolf Pack vs. UNLV football
cards.notes: Follow the annual Nevada–UNLV football matchup and view the trophy through official game coverage; do not expect the historic cannon-firing practice to occur.
cards.short_summary: The winning team possesses and paints the rivalry trophy its school color.
cards.evidence_claim: Nevada and UNLV play annually for the Fremont Cannon; the winner takes possession and paints it blue or red, while the cannon has been inoperable since 1999.
cards.access_notes: Game access and ticketing vary. The source explicitly says the cannon has been inoperable since 1999.

cards.title: Make a Homecoming-week memory
cards.subtitle: University of Nevada, Reno campus and Reno
cards.notes: Use the official Homecoming schedule when posted and choose a listed alumni, student or campus activity that fits your plans and access needs.
cards.short_summary: Homecoming connects current students with returning alumni through a longstanding campus tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: University Homecoming dates to the institution’s early years and has included football games, parades, carnival-themed games, concerts and the March from the Arch.
cards.access_notes: Events vary by year; verify the official schedule and any admission requirements before going.

cards.title: March from the Reno Arch to the Quad
cards.subtitle: Reno Arch to the University Quad during Homecoming
cards.notes: If the event returns on the official Homecoming schedule, meet at the announced downtown starting point and follow the organized route with the parade.
cards.short_summary: A Homecoming procession links downtown Reno and the historic University Quad.
cards.evidence_claim: The University described the March from the Arch as an evolved Homecoming tradition, proceeding from the Reno Arch to the University Quad.
cards.source_title: Celebrate University of Nevada, Reno Homecoming 2017
cards.access_notes: This source documents the tradition’s route and history, not a current date; confirm that it is scheduled before planning.

cards.title: Start first year in Mackay Stadium
cards.subtitle: Mackay Stadium, University of Nevada, Reno
cards.notes: Eligible first-year students should follow NevadaFIT instructions and attend the opening ceremony as part of their transition-week academic program.
cards.short_summary: NevadaFIT begins the fall semester with a stadium opening ceremony for first-year students.
cards.evidence_claim: NevadaFIT is a first-year transition program that kicks off with an outdoor opening ceremony at Mackay Stadium.
cards.access_notes: Designed for first-year students; enrollment and attendance details are set by the University for each fall term.

cards.title: See old-school mining skills in action
cards.subtitle: Mackay School of Earth Sciences and Engineering
cards.notes: Look for Mackay Muckers demonstrations or competition updates and observe the team’s skilled events through the program instead of attempting equipment-based activities alone.
cards.short_summary: The Muckers preserve mining skills through collegiate competition.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mackay Muckers practice historic mining techniques and have competed in the annual Intercollegiate Mining Games since that competition began.
cards.access_notes: Competition locations and participation are team-controlled; check current Mackay School communications for public events.

cards.title: Trace the Mackay Week legacy
cards.subtitle: Historic University of Nevada, Reno campus tradition
cards.notes: Use the University’s archival images and exhibits to learn how Mackay Day became Mackay Week, including the Manzanita Lake tug-of-war tradition.
cards.short_summary: Mackay Week grew from a 1913 event honoring the Mackay family’s support.
cards.evidence_claim: The first Mackay Day was held in 1913; it later became Mackay Week, celebrating the Mackay family and uniting campus.
cards.access_notes: Treat this as an archival tradition: the source provides history but does not confirm a current Mackay Week program.

cards.title: Listen for the Nevada Oath at welcome
cards.subtitle: New-student opening ceremony tradition
cards.notes: New students can follow their orientation schedule and join the ceremony’s guided recitation; visitors should treat it as a formal student welcome ritual.
cards.short_summary: The oath is recited alongside the Alma Mater during a new-student ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: The University identified recitation of the Nevada Oath and singing of the Alma Mater as traditions in its new-student opening ceremony.
cards.access_notes: This source documents the ceremony tradition but not a current event date; use current orientation communications for attendance details.

cards.title: Hear the Alma Mater at commencement
cards.subtitle: University of Nevada, Reno commencement
cards.notes: At a commencement ceremony, listen for the Alma Mater performed by the Wolf Pack Quartet; its archival name is “The Mackay Song.”
cards.short_summary: The University’s Alma Mater is a formal commencement tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: The University says faculty in the Wolf Pack Quartet usually sing the Alma Mater for Commencement, and its archives identify the Alma Mater as “The Mackay Song.”
cards.source_title: Tradition lives on with graduates, friends and family in mind
cards.access_notes: Commencement attendance and access are determined by the current ceremony’s official instructions.

warnings: Mackay Week and March from the Arch are included as documented traditions; the cited sources do not confirm an upcoming event date. Verify current University scheduling before planning attendance.
